context_quote: Concentrated photovoltaic-thermoelectric generator (CPV-TEG) hybrid system can harvest the low-grade waste heat derived from photovoltaic cells to generate more electric energy. However, it is economically unfeasible due to the expensive cost of thermoelectric generators and higher photovoltaics temperature. Ionic thermocell based on thermogalvanic effect has a more inexpensive cost and ionic Seebeck coefficient of 1- 2 orders of magnitude higher than thermoelectric generators, which is promising for full-spectrum solar cascade utilization. In present work, a novel concentrated photovoltaic and ionic thermocells hybrid system (CPV-iTEC) is reported, aiming to comprehensively evaluate its feasibility. The ionic thermocell adhered directly to the photovoltaic panel consists the pi-type multi-channels, electrodes and p/n-type redox electrolytes flowing in multi-channels, which can simultaneously cool photovoltaic panel and output electric energy for waste heat harvesting. A threedimensional numerical model is proposed and validated by preliminary experiment to investigate the effects of structural and operating parameters on the performance of CPV-iTEC during energy, exergy and economic analyses. Results show that the optimal structural parameters of ionic thermocell are the 2 mm channel height and 1 mm width, showing a 7.18% higher energy efficiency than that of CPV-TEG at 10 concentration ratios. The application of ionic thermocell in the full-spectrum solar cascade utilization of concentrated photovoltaic system is proved to be feasible with significant advantages of low cost, high performance, and flexible operation.

context_quote: Nanoconfinement of liquid electrolytes has been shown to exhibit an enhanced ionic Seebeck coefficient compared with bulk systems. However, experimental understanding of the underlying mechanisms remains limited, particularly for electrolytes confined within sub-nanometer nanochannels reconstructed from twodimensional (2D) layered materials. In this study, we experimentally and numerically investigate the thermoelectric response of both monovalent and multivalent liquid electrolytes in graphene oxide (GO) nanochannel membranes, using KCl as a representative system, to elucidate the governing mechanisms. An ionic Seebeck coefficient exceeding -1.2 mV/K is achieved in GO nanochannels integrated with Ag/AgCl electrodes. By isolating the thermogalvanic contribution of the electrodes, the results reveal that the observed ionic Seebeck coefficient of GO nanochannels is governed by a competition between Soret-type ion thermodiffusion and ion diffusion driven by temperature-dependent ion electrophoretic mobility (TDIEM). In the low-concentration regime, where the electrical double layer (EDL) overlap becomes significant, the TDIEM effect dominates, leading to a large negative ionic Seebeck coefficient. Continuum-based numerical simulations show qualitative agreement with experimental trends. The ionic Seebeck coefficient increases with decreasing electrolyte concentration and increasing temperature difference, accompanied by enhanced surface charge density, and reaches a maximum value of -0.400 +/- 0.038 mV/K at a KCl concentration of 0.1 mM under a temperature difference of 24 K. Moreover, monovalent electrolytes exhibit higher ionic Seebeck coefficients than multivalent electrolytes due to their higher cation mobility and lower ionic heat of transport. These findings provide new insights into nanoconfinement-enhanced ionic thermoelectricity and support the development of nanofluidic-based thermoelectric generators for low-grade heat recovery.

Self-assembled peptide composites, particularly diphenylalanine (FF) derivatives, represent a promising class of materials for such electronics due to their inherent biodegradability and ease of hybridization with functional materials. However, the integration of ionic species with these peptides is often limited by the disruption of non-covalent interactions between FF derivatives. In this study, we developed biodegradable, ionic thermoelectric composites by co-assembling Fmoc-FF with deep eutectic solvents (DESs) composed of choline chloride (ChCl) and ethylene glycol (EG). context_quote: Wearable fiber-based thermoelectric generators (TEGs) with high thermoelectric (TE) performance, mechanical property and wearing comfort are urgently needed for low-grade human body heat harvesting. Then, a wearable ionogel fiber-based wristband with synergistically improved TE performance, mechanical property and wearing comfort is prepared by a weaving process. When wearing the i-TE wristband (5-legs) at room temperature (Delta T = 2.7 K), an obviously high thermovoltage of 119.133 mV is generated, indicating its great potential as wearable energy supply devices.
